obligations.note: All four integrations at head, including the new payment-advice entry, use https base URLs. The registered exhaustive control test test_integrations_use_tls passed, unskipped, in the head-commit CI run.

The new payment-advice integration is in asset-inventory.json with owner payments-operations and data_classification npi, a listed classification; the other three integrations were already inventoried. The exhaustive test_integrations_are_inventoried passed on head; the missing purpose field is not something INV-1 requires.

Ticket CHG-26071 is standard and approved by change manager Grace Kim on 2026-10-17, before the change was opened. Its components (payments.integrations, payments.controls-data) cover both touched paths.
Mara Costa, a payments change_approver and a different person from author Jonah Weiss, gave a code_review approval.
The change has a single commit, and every approval names that head commit 7167104.

run.json shows pr-checks succeeding on head 7167104 with the full payments suite: 172 tests, 0 failures, 0 skipped. All registered control tests are present and passing, including ENC-2 and INV-1. The JUnit report's timestamp and hostname metadata look odd but do not contradict the run record.
integrations.py belongs to payments.integrations, which is security_sensitive. Ines Halvorsen, a security_reviewer, approved security_review on the head commit.
controls/payments/asset-inventory.json is a protected path. Bao Tran, a control_owner from controls-office and outside the author's payments-eng team, approved on the head commit.
This is a standard change, not an emergency one, and was not deployed before review, so no post-implementation review is due.
No deviation from a product obligation is claimed, and no exception is relied on.
No acceptance-ledger entry covers integrations.py or the asset inventory, so no prior evidence lapses. ENC-2 and INV-1 are supported by fresh head-commit control tests.

summary: The change adds one https integration, payment-advice, to the payments registry and adds a matching inventory entry with an owner and a classification. Both applicable product obligations, ENC-2 and INV-1, are satisfied by inspection and by passing exhaustive control tests on the head commit. The approved ticket covers both components. Code review, security review and control-owner approval all come from independent, correctly-roled people and name the single head commit. Every applicable obligation is shown, so the change is accepted.
